questions.stem: X = {A, B} and Y = {B, C, D}. How many attributes are in X ∪ Y?
questions.explain: The union is {A, B, C, D}. B is in both sets but is counted once.

questions.stem: The rule "if two rows agree on A, then they agree on B" is broken exactly when what happens?
options: Two rows differ on A but agree on B
Two rows differ on both A and B
Two rows agree on A but differ on B
Two rows agree on both A and B
questions.explain: An "if p then q" rule fails only when p is true and q is false: the rows agree on A, yet differ on B.

questions.stem: How many subsets, including the empty set, does {A, B, C} have?
questions.explain: Each attribute is in or out, so 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 subsets.

questions.stem: Student(roll_no, name, dept) has unique roll numbers, but names and departments repeat. Which attribute should be the primary key?
questions.explain: A key must identify each row uniquely. Only roll_no is guaranteed unique; two students can share a name and a department.

questions.stem: Students enrol in many courses and each course has many students. What is the minimum number of tables needed for Student, Course and the Enrols relationship?
questions.explain: A many-to-many relationship needs its own table, so the tables are Student, Course and Enrols.
